identification: Cast iron wall-mounted yoke bell (farm / dinner / school style), approx 30 cm mouth diameter, 50 cm overall height. Wall plate with 4 bolt holes, U-shaped hanging bracket, pivoting yoke with acorn finial, swinging pull arm for a rope, iron clapper tied with twine. Black painted finish, light rust at pivots. Pattern matches the common US farm-bell format (C.S. Bell / Hillsboro style) and the many later reproductions. Catalogue: estimate A$150-250; current bid A$220 at 10 Nov. Google Lens on photo 1: closest matches are modern 'antique style' cast iron school/dinner bells, eg The Renmy Store 'Large Cast Iron School Dinner Bell' 51 cm H x 38 cm W, 8.7 kg, A$239.95 new (same wall plate, U bracket, yoke, acorn finial and rope arm, though the lot's plate has 4 holes and a chamfered top). The clean casting, absence of any foundry name or 'No.' size mark and the twine-tied clapper point to a 20th/21st century reproduction rather than a 19th century C.S. Bell, Crystal Metal or similar US foundry bell (those carry cast names, size numbers and 1886 patent dates on the yoke). Estimated weight 8-12 kg.

viewing_check: Look on the yoke arms, the bell shoulder and inside the lip for any cast name, 'No.' size number or date (C.S. Bell, Crystal Metal, Rumsey, Goulds, Meneely, any Australian foundry). Check for 'China'/'India' marks or paper labels, check sand-casting texture (fine and even = modern), and lift it: a 30 cm cast iron bell plus bracket should be roughly 8-12 kg.
